8. The following points do arise for my consideration;
1) Whether the trial court is justified in denying ex-parte maintenance order as per I.A. No.1 and justified in dismissal of the petition as against respondent No.2 to 5 as per the impugned order dated 18/03/2024?
Crl. Appeal No.645/2024 2) Whether there is legal infirmity in the impugned order, which requires interference of this court ?
3) What Order?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The marriage and relationship of petitioner and respondents are not in dispute and it is also not in dispute that all respondent No.1 to 5 are living jointly under a common roof situated at Hyderabad.
Under the circumstances, without touching on the merits of the petition which are narrated at length, it is just and Crl.
. However, on going through the petition averments,
there are sufficient allegations against all the respondents while petitioner was staying with them in the matrimonial house.
Under the circumstances, the trial court without issuing a notice and without calling for an explanation or their answers for the alleged harassment stated to have been meted out on the petitioner, straight away dismissed the petition which is certainly not justifiable, as the very Crl.
Appeal No.645/2024 perusal of the complaint/application filed under Section 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 before the trial court discloses the abundant materials to demonstrate prima facie that there was domestic violence by respondent No.2 to 5.
Therefore, the trial court ought to have considered these points and issued notice to respondent No.2 to 5 instead of dismissing the same at first instance, therefore matter requires to be remanded on that score itself for fresh consideration.
18. In addition, though the relationship of petitioner and respondent No.1 is an admitted fact, the trial court without considering the same for an order of interim maintenance issued notice on respondent No.1/husband which is yet to be served.
Since Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is a beneficial Act enacted for the upliftment of the woman during her stay in the domestic relationship, when the relationship of the petitioner is not in Crl.
Hence, in view of the reasons assigned in the points No.1 and 2, this court opined that, without touching the merits of the case, the matter requires to be remanded to the trial court for fresh consideration in accordance with law, as such dismissal order as against respondent No.2 to 5 requires to be set aside, hence, interference by this court is very much necessary in the interest of justice.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In the written arguments submitted on behalf of respondent No.1 to 5, it is canvassed that, the order of the trial court is just and proper, there are no prima facie materials to show the commission of alleged Sonal Jain vs Rohith Jain on 9 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65219610/
6 domestic violence on the petitioner as held by the Hon'ble Apex court in case of Shyamlal Devda and others Vs. Parimala.

No.1 and 2 filed by the petitioner through CDPO and RPAD, if PF is paid and call for DIR.
